sources.title: Dubai Building Code
sources.notes: Dubai Municipality's Dubai Building Code page (last modified 15 Sep 2026) offers the 2021 edition. By A.4.1 it replaces the building-design regulations of DM, DDA, Trakhees and DSOA and incorporates or cross-references DEWA's, so it is checked first. Copyright Government of Dubai: only short paraphrases are kept here. Page numbers are PDF pages of the 843-page file; in Part G the printed page is 'G' followed by the PDF page minus 402.

sources.title: Regulations for Electrical Installations
sources.notes: DEWA's 'Circulars & Regulations' page links this edition as its Electricity Installations Regulations (checked 2026-09-17). The Dubai Building Code 2021 incorporates or cross-references it (DBC A.4.1); each clause here names the matching DBC clause. Page numbers are PDF pages of the 135-page file; the printed page number is the PDF page minus 2. Still to review: DEWA circular DP-VP-CS-GEN-0008-2022 (17 Jan 2022) on the Dubai Building Code, which DEWA's site would not serve to an automated download.

clauses.title: How the Building Code relates to other Dubai regulations
clauses.summary: The Building Code replaces the building-design regulations of Dubai Municipality, DDA, Trakhees and DSOA. DEWA's building-design regulations are built into it or cross-referenced; SIRA requirements are summarised in Part J; TRA (telecom) rules are given in G.11; and the UAE Fire & Life Safety Code is cross-referenced throughout.

clauses.title: Which edition of an international standard applies
clauses.summary: International codes and standards cited by the Building Code apply in their latest edition, unless the Code names a specific edition.

clauses.title: Basis of the electrical sections
clauses.summary: Sections G.4 to G.7 set the electrical design requirements and are based on the latest BS 7671 and IET guidance. 11 kV installations follow G.7. Anything these sections do not cover must be referred to DEWA for guidance.

clauses.title: Electrical supply characteristics
clauses.summary: DEWA supplies 230/400 V ±10%, 50 Hz, three-phase four-wire, with a separate neutral and protective conductor (normally the service cable armour). The neutral is earthed only at DEWA's substation, never inside the consumer installation. Design fault level in the substation is 40 kA for 1 s, except fuse-protected equipment. Overload, short-circuit and earth-leakage protection are required, plus protection against over-voltage, fluctuations, transients and harmonics, loss of phase and interruptions as the design needs.

clauses.title: Supply availability, substation threshold and metering
clauses.summary: Confirm with DEWA that supply is available before building design starts. If the total connected load exceeds 400 kW, space for a DEWA substation must be provided in the building or plot; one may also be required below 400 kW. Meters must meet DEWA specifications and be DEWA-approved. Where there is no building tariff meter, each tenancy needs a sub-meter, and run-hour based virtual meters are not accepted.

clauses.title: Ambient design conditions
clauses.summary: Equipment must perform in Dubai conditions: 48 °C maximum ambient in shade, 2.8 °C minimum, 37.8 °C highest 24-hour average, 26.9 °C yearly average, humidity up to 100%, 0.07 g earthquake loading, 45 m/s wind at 10 m height, 40 °C ground temperature, and soil thermal resistivity 2.0 °C·m/W at 0.9 m depth. Heavy condensation and sandstorms also occur.

clauses.title: Cable types for fixed wiring
clauses.summary: Fixed wiring normally uses LSF/XLPE-insulated stranded copper cables to one of BS 5467, 6004, 6724, 7211, 7629-1, 7846, 7889 or 8436. PVC-insulated cable needs DEWA approval. Flexible cords are LSF to BS 7211, and single-core cables armoured with steel wire or tape must not be used on AC circuits.

clauses.title: Minimum conductor sizes
clauses.summary: Lighting circuit conductors must be at least 2.5 mm², and utility socket circuit conductors at least 4 mm².

clauses.title: Current rating and voltage drop
clauses.summary: Size each cable to carry its circuit's normal current continuously for the actual laying conditions and maximum ambient temperature (BS 7769). Tables G.4 to G.6 give typical minimum sizes against breaker ratings; final selection uses manufacturers' data with correction factors and voltage drop. Voltage drop from the point of supply to any point must not exceed 4% of nominal voltage unless otherwise specified.

clauses.title: Load balancing
clauses.summary: On a three-phase supply, spread lighting, sockets, water heaters, single-phase AC units and other loads over the red, yellow and blue phases as evenly as possible at every distribution level. This clause gives no numeric limit for imbalance.

clauses.title: Water heaters, saunas, Jacuzzis and washing machines: control and isolation
clauses.summary: Control each with a suitably rated double-pole switch with neon indicator, and connect it through a flex outlet plate next to the equipment. A water heater in a bathroom or WC has its switch immediately outside the room; sauna and Jacuzzi control gear goes outside the room. Each item has its own final circuit from the DB, and every water heater circuit is protected by a 30 mA RCCB/ELCB.

clauses.title: Air-conditioning units: control and circuits
clauses.summary: Window units with cooling capacity up to 1.5 kW connect through a 15 A switched socket outlet; other room AC units need a suitably rated double-pole switch with flex outlet beside the unit. Each unit has its own final circuit. A single-phase supply may carry at most two window units; three or more are balanced over three phases. Breaker and wire are sized to the unit's load, with a minimum of 20 A and 4 mm².

clauses.title: Assessing lighting and small-power loads
clauses.summary: Lighting and fan circuits: at most 2,000 W, at least 2.5 mm² LSF wire and ECC, breaker at most 16 A. Where fittings are not yet chosen, allow at least 100 W per lighting or fan point; fluorescent lamps count as 1.8 times lamp watts. A radial circuit serves up to five 13 A sockets (not in kitchens) on a 20 A breaker; a ring serves up to ten on 30 A. Count each 13 A socket circuit as 13 A demand and each general 13 A socket as at least 200 W (a twin counts as two). General-purpose 15 A sockets may be taken as 500 W each in residential premises (1,000 W commercial or industrial). Fixed appliances and AC use actual load; items of 5 VA or less may be left out.

clauses.title: Maximum demand and DEWA schedule formats
clauses.summary: Every DB is rated for its total connected load before any demand factor. A final circuit's demand is the higher of the actual or assumed point loads, with diversity where appropriate. A qualified engineer may set the demand factor at main and sub-main level, and it must not exceed 1. Load distribution schedules go to DEWA in the formats of Tables G.11 to G.14; per the note to Table G.11, total connected load includes standby, spare and future provisions.

clauses.title: Maximum demand allowed at an MDB (no large motors)
clauses.summary: For normal residential and commercial premises without large motor loads, the maximum demand allowed at an MDB is 30 kW on a 60 A feeder, 50 kW on 100 A, 60 kW on 125 A, 80 kW on 160 A, 100 kW on 200 A, 150 kW on 300 A, 200 kW on 400 A, 800 kW on a 1,000 kVA transformer and 1,200 kW on a 1,500 kVA transformer.

clauses.title: Connected-load limits with motor and AC loads
clauses.summary: Where DEWA transformers feed motors and AC with no single load above 100 kW, connected load is limited to 950 kW on a 1,500 kVA transformer and 650 kW on 1,000 kVA. Any single load above 100 kW needs DEWA approval, judged on rating, starter type, starting current, number of compressors or motors and operating stages. LV panel and MDB incomer protection is set at the design current. Other maximum-demand methods are allowed if the method and the diversity at each level are submitted to DEWA and shown on the drawings and schedules.

clauses.title: Recommended RCD (ELCB/RCCB) operating currents
clauses.summary: Recommended residual operating currents: 30 mA for 13 A sockets, water heaters, coolers, dishwashers, fridges, washing machines, domestic water pumps and general-purpose 15 A sockets; 10 mA for Jacuzzi pumps and underwater lighting; 30/100 mA general lighting; 100/300 mA flood lighting; 100 mA window or split AC, FCU/AHU/VAV, irrigation pumps and cookers; 100/300 mA package AC units and industrial machines; 100/500/1,000 mA chillers; 300/500 mA lifts, escalators and hoists; 300 mA neon signs. Confirm against the manufacturer's recommendations. Circuits may be grouped under one RCD, and fire-protection equipment that needs an uninterrupted supply should have an earth-leakage detection system with indication or alarm.

clauses.title: Power factor correction and capacitor banks
clauses.summary: Installation power factor must stay between 0.9 lagging and unity; 0.95 lagging is recommended. AC units, motors and discharge lighting must be corrected to at least 0.95 lagging. Where individual correction is not achieved, automatic stepped capacitor banks at main or sub-main level are required: for commercial premises on DEWA feeders of 200 A and above, and for residential premises the threshold is a 400 A feeder. Capacitors must be dry sealed units to IEC 61921, temperature class D, with automatic discharge, overcurrent protection for each bank, means of isolation and switching-duty contactors. A network study must check for resonance, and series harmonic filter reactors are tuned below the lowest harmonic present.

clauses.title: Electric supply (see DBC G.4.2)
clauses.summary: Same supply characteristics as the Building Code G.4.2: 230/400 V ±10%, 50 Hz, three-phase four-wire with separate neutral and protective conductor; neutral earthed only at DEWA's substation; substation design fault level 40 kA for 1 s, except fuse-protected equipment.

clauses.title: Substation provision (see DBC G.4.3)
clauses.summary: Where total connected load exceeds 400 kW, space for a DEWA substation must be provided in the building or plot; one may be needed below 400 kW. The requirement is confirmed in DEWA's No Objection Certificate, which must be revalidated when its stated period ends.

clauses.title: Cable rating and voltage drop (see DBC G.4.7.3)
clauses.summary: Cables must carry their circuit's normal current continuously for the laying conditions and maximum ambient (BS 7769); Appendix 5, Tables 1 to 3, give typical minimum selections. Voltage drop from the point of supply to any equipment must not exceed 4% of nominal voltage unless otherwise specified.

clauses.title: Control of air-conditioning units (compare DBC G.4.13.8)
clauses.summary: Window units with cooling capacity up to 18,000 Btu/hour connect through a 15 A switched socket outlet; other room units need a suitably rated double-pole switch with flex outlet beside the unit. Each unit has its own final circuit; at most two window units per single-phase supply; breaker and wire sized to the load with a minimum of 20 A and 4 mm². The Building Code G.4.13.8 states the socket limit as 1.5 kW instead of 18,000 Btu/hour, so confirm which figure applies.

clauses.title: Maximum demand limits (see DBC Tables G.15 and G.16)
clauses.summary: DBs are rated for total connected load before any demand factor, which a qualified engineer works out; schedules follow Appendices 2 to 4. Guidance limits for maximum demand at an MDB without large motors: 30 kW on 60 A, 50 kW on 100 A, 60 kW on 125 A, 80 kW on 160 A, 100 kW on 200 A, 150 kW on 300 A, 200 kW on 400 A, 800 kW on a 1,000 kVA transformer and 1,200 kW on 1,500 kVA. With motor or AC loads each up to 100 kW, connected load is limited to 950 kW (1,500 kVA) or 650 kW (1,000 kVA); larger single loads need approval.

clauses.title: Earth-leakage alarms for fire and essential pumps
clauses.summary: Fire pumps, jockey pumps, submersible pumps, sump pumps and other essential equipment need earth-leakage sensors or relays with alarm or indication, set to warn before a fault condition is reached.

clauses.title: Power factor correction (see DBC G.4.20.1)
clauses.summary: Installation power factor between 0.9 lagging and unity, 0.95 recommended; AC units, motors and discharge lighting corrected to 0.95 lagging or better. Automatic stepped capacitor banks at main or sub-main level where individual correction is not achieved: commercial premises on feeders of 200 A and above, and residential premises at a 400 A feeder. Capacitors are dry sealed units to IEC 61921, temperature class D, with automatic discharge. Section 1.9 of the same document gives 0.9 as the minimum for AC equipment.

clauses.title: Recommended RCD operating currents (see DBC Table G.21)
clauses.summary: The same recommended ELCB/RCCB operating currents as Building Code Table G.21: 30 mA for 13 A sockets, water heaters, washing machines, domestic pumps and general 15 A sockets; 10 mA for Jacuzzi pumps and underwater lighting; 100 mA for window or split AC, FCU/AHU/VAV, irrigation pumps and cookers; 300 mA for neon signs; ranges for lighting, package AC, chillers, lifts and industrial machines. Grouping of circuits under one device is permitted.

clauses.title: Transformer diversity factors by load type
clauses.summary: For transformer demand, apply 0.8 to chillers; 0.6 to FAHUs and pumps (plumbing, chilled-water pump sets) and lifts; 0.4 to retail loads; and 0.3 to all other loads.

clauses.title: Maximum demand allowed per transformer rating
clauses.summary: Maximum demand is restricted to 1,147 kW on a 1,500 kVA transformer, 956 kW on 1,250 kVA, 765 kW on 1,000 kVA, 482 kW on 630 kVA and 382 kW on 500 kVA. The transformer size is decided from the load detail.

clauses.ref: Armoured and unarmoured PVC sheathed cables
clauses.title: Voltage drop per ampere per metre, PVC-sheathed cables
clauses.summary: Voltage drop per ampere per metre for armoured and unarmoured PVC-sheathed cables: 10 mm² 4.8; 16 mm² 2.5; 25 mm² 1.65; 35 mm² 1.15; 50 mm² 0.87; 70 mm² 0.6; 95 mm² 0.45; 120 mm² 0.37; 150 mm² 0.3; 185 mm² 0.26; 240 mm² 0.21; 300 mm² 0.185 mV/A/m.

clauses.title: Voltage drop per ampere per metre, single-core wires in conduit
clauses.summary: Voltage drop per ampere per metre for single-core wires in conduit (as identified by the user): 2.5 mm² 19; 4 mm² 12; 6 mm² 7.9; 10 mm² 4.7; 16 mm² 2.9 mV/A/m.

clauses.ref: Main CB rating vs earth electrodes
clauses.title: Earth electrodes and earth conductor by main breaker rating
clauses.summary: Minimum number of earth electrodes and earth conductor size by main breaker rating: 60–100 A one electrode, 16 mm²; 200–300 A one, 50 mm²; 400 A one, 70 mm²; 500–1,600 A two, 70 mm²; 2,000–2,500 A two, 150 mm².

clauses.title: Meter type, CT ratio, cable length and load
clauses.summary: CT meters: 100/5 A up to 55 kW with at most 12 m from meter to CT; 200/5 A up to 110 kW, 300/5 A up to 160 kW and 600/5 A up to 350 kW with 25 m; 1,000/5 A up to 550 kW and 1,600/5 A up to 800 kW with 40 m; 2,000/5 A above 800 kW (1,500 kVA transformer); 2,500/5 A and 3,000/5 A special cases referred to DEWA's metering section. Direct meters: single-phase up to 9 kW and three-phase up to 52 kW, cable at most 25 mm². A check meter is required above 900 kW (1 MVA transformer).

clauses.ref: Main CB rating vs room dimensions
clauses.title: Electrical room size by main breaker rating
Demand factors in the worked example of a main distribution board
clauses.summary: The worked example applies 0.90 to the landlord-services and external-lighting final distribution boards (type SM), 0.85 to floor sub-main boards, 0.66 to the MCC, 0.90 to running chillers, 0.50 to lifts and the jockey pump, and 0 to standby or emergency equipment such as the standby chiller and sprinkler pump.

clauses.title: Demand factors by load type for the load schedule
clauses.summary: Residential SMDBs 0.70; pumps including chilled-water pumps 0.80 (standby pumps are left out of diversity); AHUs and OAHUs 0.90; passenger lifts 0.80; service and fireman lifts 0.90; substation DB 1.0; EV charger SMDBs 0.90; EMDBs 0.90; extract and make-up fans 0.90; irrigation pumps 0.50; swimming pool 0.80. Spare ways count in full at their own panel and at 0.8 when aggregated at the main distribution board.
